definition_context: SFinite μ means μ is a countable sum of finite measures. IsSFiniteKernel means the corresponding countable decomposition as finite kernels. These are not probability, sigma-finiteness or finite total mass hypotheses.

A Kernel X Y assigns a measure on Y to each x with measurable event evaluations. F.comap (fun b => (a,b)) restricts the jointly measurable update to the measurable inclusion of the fiber with fixed first coordinate a.

μ ⊗ₘ R is the comp-product joint measure whose nonnegative integral integrates b against R a and then a against μ. ×ₖ is the pointwise product of kernels. Kernel.deterministic Prod.fst measurable_fst returns a Dirac mass at the input first coordinate, so its product with F retains that coordinate.

Kernel.IsReversible K μ means for every pair of measurable sets S,T equality of the extended nonnegative flux integrals from S to T and from T to S. It does not require Markovness, finite flux or invariance.
cases.statement:
example
    {A B : Type*} [MeasurableSpace A] [MeasurableSpace B]
    (μ : Measure A) [SFinite μ]
    (R : Kernel A B) [IsSFiniteKernel R]
    (F : Kernel (A × B) B) [IsSFiniteKernel F]
    (hF : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, (F.comap (fun b => (a, b))
      (measurable_const.prodMk measurable_id)).IsReversible (R a)) :
    ((Kernel.deterministic Prod.fst measurable_fst) ×ₖ F).IsReversible (μ ⊗ₘ R)
